messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: PD#67891 — Dedicated inference pool 'zenith-eu-west-1' high 5xx rate (threshold 5%) — triggered at 2024-05-22T12:05:08Z. Impacting customers with reserved capacity: Zenith Health, Kestrel Finance.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Responders: @alex.sre (primary), @naomi.oncall (secondary). Escalation started.

alex.sre: on it, joining zoom. starting quick triage — checking autoscaler + node health.

naomi.oncall: paging routing shows repeated tail latencies and 502s from inference nodes 10-13.

marcus.backend: seeing model worker OOMs and grpc short reads in the runtime logs for `redwood-open-7b-q4`. sample log:```
[E] 12:06:32 runtime.cu: kvcache_reclaim failed: cudaMalloc( ) OOM
[E] 12:06:33 http: write tcp 10.0.3.12:443->...: write: broken pipe
```

alex.sre: good catch. OOM pattern + connection resets = probable degraded nodes. I'm removing nodes 11-13 from routing, will spin new nodes.

ops-sre: tagging related dedicated autoscaler history — recent deploy 2h ago changed CUDA kernel selector; rolling back might be needed.

emily.incidentmgr: @lisa-csm can you start the enterprise notifications queue? we need an email + status page blurb for Zenith and Kestrel — tailored impact and contacts.

lisa-csm: drafting now. have Zenith contact list:
- Dr. Priya Rao (Primary) — priya@zenithhealth.com, +1-415-555-0198 (pager)
- Tom Alvarez (Infra Lead) — tom.alvarez@zenithhealth.com, +44 7700 900123
- Support alias — infra@zenithhealth.com
Kestrel contacts:
- ops@kestrel.finance, account manager: jennifer.k@kestrel.finance

lisa-csm: proposed tailored impact statement for Zenith: \"We are investigating elevated request failures (20-40% 5xx) and increased median inference latency for your dedicated pool in eu-west-1. Some model requests are failing to complete between 12:05–12:35 UTC. Our engineers have removed unhealthy nodes and enabled temporary fallback routing to hosted pools to reduce failures. We will provide follow-ups every 15 minutes and a post-incident summary.\"

emily.incidentmgr: looks good; can you add explicit guidance on what we've done and recommended customer actions? e.g., avoid large batch jobs, hold non-urgent scheduled jobs.

lisa-csm: updated: added recommended actions for Zenith: suspend large batch runs, switch non-critical traffic to hosted endpoint, expect degraded throughput while we rebalance.

marcus.backend: mitigation steps in progress: 
1) drain nodes 11-13 from load balancer:```sh
$ infractl node drain --pool zenith-eu-west-1 --node 11,12,13
```
2) scale up pool by +3 nodes with older kernel:```sh
$ infractl pool resize --pool zenith-eu-west-1 --delta 3 --image runtime:v1.27-fallback
```
3) enable fallback routing policy to hosted with throttled rate:```json
{"policy":"fallback-hosted","max_rps":200}
```

naomi.oncall: executing drain now. Marcus — please confirm autoscaler roll forward after we validate new nodes healthy.

alex.sre: quick status update for internal comms (15:12 UTC): removed 3 unhealthy nodes, initiated scale-up, fallback routing enabled — good partial reduction in 5xx (observed drop from 34% -> 12%). still above threshold.

incident-bot: Statuspage draft v1 generated: 
- Component: Dedicated inference (eu-west-1) — Degraded Performance
- Impact: Some customers with reserved capacity may experience increased error rates (5xx) and higher latency.
- Update: Engineering has removed unhealthy nodes and enabled fallback routing to hosted pools. Active mitigation in progress.
- Next update: in 15 minutes.

emily.incidentmgr: Alex — paste the short status page text we can publish to public status. Keep it non-account-specific except for enterprise DM.

alex.sre: public status blurb: \"We are investigating elevated errors and latency affecting dedicated inference in eu-west-1. Engineers have identified degraded nodes and are performing remedial actions, including removing unhealthy machines and enabling fallback routing to hosted pools. We will provide updates as mitigation progresses.\"

lisa-csm: prepping enterprise email for Zenith now. Draft below — please review/edit: 
Subject: Incident affecting your dedicated inference pool in eu-west-1 (Zenith Health)

Hi Priya / Tom,

We’re investigating elevated failures and latency for your dedicated inference pool in eu-west-1 that began at ~12:05 UTC. Impact: approx 20-40% of requests returned 5xx and some requests timed out between 12:05–12:35 UTC.

What we’ve done so far:
- Removed three unhealthy nodes from your pool.
- Scaled the pool with fallback runtime and enabled routed traffic to hosted pools for critical requests.
- Monitoring for error rate reduction and will provide updates every 15 minutes.

Recommended customer actions:
- Pause large batch jobs until we confirm stability.
- If you need immediate availability, switch critical requests to the hosted endpoint (we can provide a short-lived API key if needed).

Owner: Lisa (CSM), Engineering lead: Alex.

We will follow up shortly with a status update.

Best,
Lisa & Redwood Support

marcus.backend: small note — for hosted fallback we've rate-limited to 200rps to protect shared pools. If Zenith needs higher, we can negotiate dedicated burst.

naomi.oncall: monitoring metrics — error rate now 8–10% after scale up, latency p95 still elevated (~1.4s vs baseline 0.6s).

emily.incidentmgr: ok publish public status page with Alex's blurb. Lisa — send enterprise email to Zenith contacts and CC Jen for Kestrel team to evaluate. Make sure we include the contact alias for legal if they want a formal SOC note.

lisa-csm: sending now. copying draft to thread: ```
To: priya@zenithhealth.com, tom.alvarez@zenithhealth.com
Subject: [Redwood] Incident affecting dedicated inference — eu-west-1
[...body as above...]
```

incident-bot: Email to Zenith sent at 12:22 UTC (ID: mail_98321).

naomi.oncall: quick note for on-call handoff: I'll remain until 13:00 UTC, then hand off to @marcus.backend for the 13:00–17:00 shift. Marcus confirm you can take?

marcus.backend: confirmed, I'll be on-call handoff receiver and will continue mitigation check & postmortem capture.

ops-sre: we should queue a rollback of runtime:v1.28 -> v1.26 for candidate nodes, leaving new nodes on fallback runtime only. Marcus, can you own change control?

marcus.backend: I will own the change control, will coordinate with infra for a controlled rollback and post-deploy smoke tests.

alex.sre: TL;DR current status at 12:45 UTC: 5xx reduced to 6-9%, new nodes healthy, p95 latency improving but not back to baseline. Published public status. Enterprise notifications sent to Zenith & Kestrel. Owner assignments set.

emily.incidentmgr: good. next update 13:00 UTC (handoff) with post-mitigation verification. Add item: create customer-facing post-incident report and estimated root cause (kernel selector regression vs memory leak). Marcus owns PIR.

lisa-csm: noted. I'll coordinate the customer post-mortem distribution list.

incident-bot: Update scheduled: next automated reminder in 15 minutes.

[13:02 UTC] naomi.oncall: handoff complete. Marcus taking over. leaving notes pinned: drain commands, mail id, statuspage id. :thumbsup:

marcus.backend: confirmed, continuing to monitor. beginning controlled rollback on a small subset of nodes for verification — will post results.

[13:35 UTC] marcus.backend: rollback successful on test subset; observed further drop in errors to ~2-3% and p95 trending to 0.8s. promoting rollback to remainder with staged deploy.

[14:05 UTC] incident-bot: Incident resolved (partial) — error rates returned near baseline for Zenith after staged rollback & node replacement. Remaining follow-ups: full post-incident report, billing impact review (customers with retries may have higher token usage), and confirm any legal/compliance notifications for enterprise contracts.

emily.incidentmgr: great work. marking incident: COMPLETED — will convert to PIR and schedule review with infra and runtime leads. Thanks everyone.

lisa-csm: sending final wrap email to Zenith summarizing actions and next steps. will include timeline and owner contacts.

alex.sre: adding remediation checklist to the incident ticket: add kernel selector test to CI, memory-pressure tests for runtime, autoscaler safeguards to avoid removing too many nodes simultaneously.

ops-sre: capturing all logs and attaching to postmortem.

marcus.backend: PIR ticket created: PIR-2024-178 (assigned to me).

incident-bot: Thread closed by Emily at 14:07 UTC.
